text.p: Blue-chip stocks dipped Friday, taking a breather after a scorching run by the Dow Jones industrial average to 7,000, on profit-taking and investor reluctance ahead of a three-day weekend.
The Dow, the world's most widely watched stock index, was down 21.17 points at 7,001.27 just after 1 p.m. EST after crossing the 7,000 mark for the first time Thursday.
"The bond market has stalled out, and stocks have not done well all day long, despite favourable economic data today," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at brokerage First Albany Corp.
On the broader market, advances led declines 12 to 11 on active volume of 296 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

"We have reached a level at which you see a solid round of profit-taking. It indicates that the advance has been narrow and that the breadth, except for yesterday, has not been stellar," Johnson said.
The Nasdaq Composite Index was down 5.70 at 1,365.11.
In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was up more than a quarter point, sending its yield down to 6.55 percent vs. 6.63 percent.
Bonds rallied after a unexpected 0.3 percent drop in January wholesale prices as well as lower than forecast January industrial production and capacity utilization data.
Johnson said the market has maintained a defensive slant despite its advance, with defensive stocks like banks and some consumer companies among the stocks in the forefront.
Grace Messner, vice president in charge of equity management at Wilmington Trust, said the lack of a strong correction in the stock market was a cause for concern.
"I feel the same way I felt three weeks ago," Messner said. "We have run too far too fast, and I find it amazing that we continue not to have a correction," Messner said.

"A correction is sorely needed. We need a good consolidation period. The market is very vulnerable to any problems on the horizon," she said. "The only problem I can see, though, is that profit margins appeared to have peaked for the world as a whole."

Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross, said that since the market's advance was being driven by a narrow list of stocks, it had to take a breather after any big move higher.

"This is a market which built its momentum simply by having money thrown at it," Blumberg said. "But people who are rational investors don't go chasing just any stocks, they don't follow the bandwagon, so you get these lulls."

Among Friday's special situations, International Business Machines Corp. dropped after Gruntal & Co. said it trimmed its first-quarter and full-year earnings estimates for the company. IBM was down 5/8 at 145-1/2.

Micron Technology Inc. topped the NYSE most active list, rising 1-1/4 to 34-1/8 following a forecast by the company late Thursday it would record a second-quarter gain from a secondary offering for Micron Electronics Inc.
